evidence: Source review of the frozen bytes; this row needs no runtime measurement, and none is claimed. (1) Name vs slug: task.toml:5 `name = "turing/hireops-recruiting-operations"`; the manifest's task path is projects/hireops-recruiting-operations/hireops-recruiting-operations, so name == turing/<dirname>, org is turing as the delivery profile requires, and the slug has 3 hyphen tokens (check-task-slug limit). The snapshot directory being called `task` is excluded by the assignment. (2) Description, task.toml:6: "Recruiting and compensation operations with exact valuation, tiered approvals, netted multi-offer transfers, stale previews, atomic settlement, durable retry receipts and a live multi-member change desk." Each axis maps to the brief: instruction.md para 1 (netted exchange between fully committed requisitions, one commit posting all or none), para 2 (out-of-date preview refused, retry returns the original receipt after restart), para 3 (tiered approvals, exact equity valuation), paras 4-5 (change desk with two to four hires, self-updating within fifteen seconds). (3) Keywords, task.toml:7 `["recruiting", "compensation", "ledger", "webdev", "turing", "full-stack"]`: carries the three template-fixed keywords plus domain terms; `ledger` is grounded in hireops_rules.md:87 ("A signed ledger adjustment may be negative") and :93. (4) Metadata: difficulty = "hard" (allowed value); difficulty_explanation (task.toml:11) describes the same product: netted multi-offer transfer, intervening-history detection "even after balances return" (brief para 2), receipt replay after restart, UTC calendar boundaries (rules:294), signed bonus adjustments (rules:87), member removal, what-if for roles that cannot save, unsent entries across reload and ended session, follow-other-people's-changes without disturbing typing/focus/scroll (brief paras 4-6); category = "programming" and tags equal the template values; provenance = "Adapted from the supplied HireOps task ..." names this product; arena_slice = "recruiting-hiring-operations" matches the domain. (5) Agreement with other identity surfaces: tests/app_context.md:3 `Name: HireOps`; golden package.json name "hireops", index.html title "HireOps — offer & clawback desk"; brief opens "Can you build HireOps into a compensation change desk?". (6) No residue: grep of the frozen task for CHANGE_ME, change-me and sibling product names (colderwater, bazaarbridge, torquebay, expenseflow, medcare, gridforge, patchpad) returned nothing. (7) No criterion count is quoted in description or provenance, so the contract's 'quoted criterion counts' agreement (staged-task-contract.md:181) has nothing to drift against (actual blocks: functional 152, polish 5, visual 5, gates 1+1). (8) [task].version absent, which the row allows. Adversarial reading: a description copied from a sibling or left stale from the pre-change-desk version would fail this row; the description and difficulty_explanation both name the live change desk added in this candidate, so they are current. Non-blocking observations, none a defect under the workbook wording: (a) the description identifies the product by domain and never uses the word HireOps (the name field and provenance do); quality-checks.md:40 says the description 'names this product', so adding the name would remove any doubt; (b) the contract's comment at staged-task-contract.md:42 lists 'judge, dimension policy' as description content and the description omits both; the template itself only says CHANGE_ME and omission avoids a drift source; (c) arena_slice has no stack prefix, unlike most sibling tasks in projects/ (e.g. full-stack-node-express-sqlite-torquebay-repair-operations); neither workbook nor skill prescribes a slice format, and I found no suite domain plan in the frozen rules to compare against, so the slice value's conformance to an external plan is unverified; (d) the last sentence of difficulty_explanation, "Useful outcomes receive independent credit.", describes grading policy rather than difficulty; harmless in metadata that the agent does not see.
